result.topic_en: Euler tests whether N = 1000003 is prime by writing it as 3·577² + 19·8², setting 1000003 − 3xx = 19yy, and splitting the resulting equation into sub-cases A, B, C and D, then searching each for square values.
result.transcription:
=== 20 ===

posteriori autem hujus numeri examine intelligere licet, in genere eo majus lucrum exspectari posse, quo majores numeros pro $\alpha$ et $\beta$ accipere liceat.

Exemplum 2.

§. 28. Propositus sit numerus $N = 1000003$, qui manifesto continetur in formula: $3 \cdot 1^2 + 1 \cdot 1000^2$. Quoniam autem, uti modo monuimus, expedit pro $\alpha$ et $\beta$ numeros majores adhibere, idem quoque numerus facile repertus est contineri in forma $3 \cdot 577^2 + 19 \cdot 8^2$, ita ut sit $\alpha = 3$ et $\beta = 19$, ideoque $\alpha\beta = 57$, qui numerus, uti commode evenit, inter idoneos jam supra est relatus. Hanc ob rem statuamus $1000003 - 3xx = 19yy$ atque ipsi $x$ talis valor tribui debet, ut formula haec divisionem per numerum 19 admittat. Quare cum in casu cognito sit $x = 577 = 30 \cdot 19 + 7$, ponamus hic $x = 7 + 19z$, et facta divisione per 19 orietur haec aequatio: $52624 - 42z - 57zz = yy$. Ubi statim duo casus considerandi occurrunt prouti $z$ fuerit numerus par vel impar. Pro priori casu statuatur $z = 2a$, et aequatio per 4 divisa ita se habebit: $13156 - 21a - 57aa = \frac{yy}{4}$, quam vocemus $= A$. Pro altero casu ponatur $z = 4b - 1$, quoniam facile est videre, valorem $z = 4b + 1$ penitus excludi. Hinc ergo oritur haec altera aequatio principalis:
$B = 52609 + 288b - 912bb = yy$.
Has igitur duas aequationes A et B, principales, seorsim ulterius evolvamus.

Evolutio Formulae
$A = 13156 - 21a - 57aa = \frac{yy}{4}$.

§. 29. Hic subdivisio in duos alios casus institui debet, quorum quisque iterum seorsim evolvatur. Sit primo $a$ nu-
merus

=== 31 ===

merus par, et quidem $a = 4c$, qui valor, in aequatione A substitutus, producit sequentem aequationem, postquam scilicet divisio per 4 fuerit facta: $C = 3289 - 21c - 228cc = \frac{yy}{16}$.
Hic ergo a numero absoluto 3289 successive subtrahi debent numeri in forma $228cc + 21c$ contenti, qui sunt:
si $c$ numerus negativus: 207, 870, 1989
si $c$ numerus positivus: 249, 954, 2115
unde autem nullum quadratum resultat.

§. 30. Sumamus ergo pro $a$ numerum imparem, qui manifesto debet esse formae $4d - 1$. Facta igitur substitutione $a = 4d - 1$, simulque divisione per 4, orietur haec aequatio: $D = 3280 + 93d - 228dd$. Hinc numeri formae $228dd \pm 93d$ a numero absoluto 3280 successive subtrahendi erunt
si $d$ numerus negativus: 135, 726, 1773, 3276
si $d$ numerus positivus: 321, 1098, 2331
quorum quartus prioris seriei dat quadratum 4 ex casu $d = -4$, unde fit $y = 8$, qui casus jam est cognitus, praeter quem hic nullum amplius quadratum occurrit.

Evolutio Formulae
$B = 52609 + 288b - 912bb = yy$.

§. 31. Hic ergo a numero absoluto 52609 successive subtrahantur numeri in formula $912bb \pm 288b$ contenti, quos hic in gemina columna, una cum eorum differentiis, tam pro valoribus ipsius $b$ positivis quam negativis repraesentemus:

$b$ | $912bb - 288b$ | Diff. || $b$ | $912bb + 288b$ | Diff.
0 | 0 | || 0 | 0 |
1 | 624 | 624 || 1 | 1200 | 1200
2 | 3072 | 2448 || 2 | 4224 | 3024
3 | 7344 | 4272 || 3 | 9072 | 4848

items.english: Let the proposed number be N = 1000003 (to be examined for primality).

items.quote: quoniam facile est videre, valorem $z = 4b + 1$ penitus excludi
items.english: since it is easy to see that the value z = 4b + 1 is entirely excluded.
from which, however, no square results.

items.quote: quorum quartus prioris seriei dat quadratum 4 ex casu $d = -4$, unde fit $y = 8$, qui casus jam est cognitus, praeter quem hic nullum amplius quadratum occurrit.
items.english: of which the fourth of the first series gives the square 4 from the case d = −4, whence y = 8; this case is already known, and apart from it no further square occurs here.

items.quote: Has igitur duas aequationes A et B, principales, seorsim ulterius evolvamus.
items.english: Let us therefore develop these two principal equations A and B further, separately.
